- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for negative sentiment.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 2–5 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after sentiment spikes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 7-day average is >1.5x historical mean, reduce forecast by 15–25%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to overcorrect; apply a smoothing filter to dampen extreme swings.
- In high-sentiment + high-forecast scenarios, model often fails to account for regulatory or policy shocks; add a 5–10% downward buffer if sentiment >0.75 and price >3.0.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >20% in 3 consecutive days, apply a 10–15% downward adjustment to next forecast.
